title: The Genealogy Stall That Sells Nothing

features.name: the kinship register
features.desc-on-touch: charts drawn in a hand you recognize: all the names that ever belonged to someone, no price attached. you trace your finger down a column and realize you were always here.

features.name: the unstocked counter
features.desc-on-touch: empty shelves behind glass, waiting. what was never made to be sold sits here anyway, teaching.

features.name: the maker's thumbprint
features.desc-on-touch: pressed into the corner of one chart: a mark that says this genealogy was built by someone with fingers. you know who. you have always known.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the quiet work of naming
narr: you sat across from her at a table, watching her
hand move through the columns. she was writing names
that never made ledgers, never cost anything. when she
pressed her thumb to mark a corner, you saw the whole
work: kinship that asked for nothing but knowing.

inscription: every good remains in conversation with the hand that made it, and so does every name

file.name: Genealogy_Market_Unnamed_Generations_Unnumbered.ledger
file.note: a ledger of kinships that were never goods, only truths the stall keeper knew without selling

exits.label: back through the market rows where names become stories
into the sparse air where only naming survives
toward makers who left no names but left fingerprints
